title: Causes and effects of inequality
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers only the costs and benefits of inequality, while the new point also needs its causes (skills, jobs, inheritance and age), which no bank point teaches, so it would need a new point.

draft.title: Causes and effects of inequality
card: Income and wealth differ between people for many reasons. Skills and education matter: workers with more skills and qualifications often earn higher wages.
The type of job matters too, as some jobs pay more than others. Age matters because older people have usually had more years to save and build wealth.
Inheritance passes wealth from one generation to the next. A person who inherits a house starts with assets that others must save for years to buy.

Too much inequality can harm social cohesion, which is how well people in a society trust and get along with each other. It can also slow economic growth if many people cannot afford education or health care.
draft.remember: Skills, jobs, age and inheritance drive inequality. Too much can weaken cohesion and growth.

a.q: Which of these is an example of inheritance causing wealth inequality?
opts: Lena receives a house from her grandmother
Lena earns a high wage as a surgeon
Lena saves part of her pay for 30 years
a.why: Inheritance is wealth passed on from another person, so Lena starts with an asset she did not earn. The surgeon's wage comes from skills and a job, and saving over 30 years is linked to age.
a.clue: Which one is wealth handed on by someone else?

b.q: In a town, many families cannot afford to send their children to school or see a doctor. Why might this slow economic growth?
opts: Fewer people build skills and good health to work
Higher wages push up the cost of making goods
Wealthy families spend less on their own homes
Older workers have saved more than younger workers
b.why: When many people miss out on education and health care, the workforce has fewer skills and poorer health, and this can slow growth. Age and savings explain differences in wealth, but they do not explain this effect.
b.clue: Think about what education and health give to workers.

a.best: Lena receives a house from her grandmother

b.best: Fewer people build skills and good health to work
